Source: venom gland, South American pit vipers, Crotalus durissus terrificus
Activity: Anti-Gram+ & Gram-, Antifungal, Synergistic AMPs, Hemolytic, Anticancer
Additional info: Sequence analysis: 85.29% similar to AP896 BF-CATH. Activity: active against Gram+ E. faecalis ATCC 29212 and a clinical isolate (MIC 7.7-31 uM), S. aureus ATCC 29213 and a clinical isolate (MIC 7.7 uM), S. pyogenes clinical isolate (MIC 3.8 uM), Gram- P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 and a clinical isolate (MIC 0.24-3.8 uM), K. pneumoniae clinical isolate (MIC 1.9 uM), E. coli ATCC 25922 and a clinical isolate (MIC 0.06-3.8 uM), and A. baumannii clinical isolate (MIC 3.8 uM). Fungi: active against yeasts C-parapsilosis ATCC 22019 (MIC>40 uM), C. krusei ATCC 6258 (MIC 40 uM), C. tropicalis LABMIC 0109 (MIC 10-40 uM), C. albicans LABMIC 0107 or 0108 (MIC 20-40 uM), C. parapsilosis LABMIC 0113 (MIC 2.5 uM), C. laurentii LABMIC 0404 (MIC 20 uM), Dermatophythes M. canis LABMIC 0401 (MIC 1.25 uM), T. rubrum LABMIC 0203 or 0204 (MIC 5 uM) (Cavalcante et al., 2017). Appeared to have proinflammatory effect on immune cells such as Raw 264.7 cells (Oliveira-Júnior et al., 2018). Half-life in vitro:serum:human: half-life 71 min (50% serum). Structure: residues 3-21 are helical when bound to DPC micelles. You can rotate, zoom, and view the crystal structure of BPTI in complex with trypsin here in the PDB. Ctn is toxic to cancer cells HeLa S3 and U937, in the low uM range for THP-1 (IC50 ~1.56 uM) and MM6 (IC50 3.12 uM), and above 12.5 uM for HL-60 and Jurkat E6.1. SAR: Like LL-37, the N-terminal fragment Ctn[1-14] has weak activity, while the c-terminal fragment Ctn[15-34] is antibacterial and antitumor with increased cell selectivity (Falcao CB et al., 2015). Toxicity: Ctn was the most active peptide against dermatophytes. Toxic to human fibroblasts (IC50 6.25 uM) and also the most toxic to healthy eukaryotic cells. Human RBC: HC50 < 100 uM. Fragments Ctn[1–14] and Ctn[15–35] lost activity against dermatophytes, but became more active against pathogenic yeasts, including several Candida species, both clinical isolates and standard strains, with MICs as low as 5 uM (Cavalcante CS et al., 2016). Synergy:drug: it showed synergistic antifungal activity with amphotericin B (FICI 0.26) (Cavalcante et al., 2017). Reg. 8/2014; Update 4/2016; 11/2016; 7/2021; 12/2024 GW.

SAR: a 12mer of the alpha7 helix, retaining a full three turns of the alpha-helix and ending with cysteine-167, is as effective in protecting against C. albicans infection in the worm model and inhibiting surface adhesion as full-length EntV. Its toxicity relies on an internal 10 kDa peptide (pepcanatox), released by hydrolysis of Canatoxin by cathepsins in the digestive system of susceptible insects. Shown here is the 93 amino acid fragment recombinantly expressed for biological and structural analysis (The six-residue His tag was omitted). It is insecticidal (e.g. S. frugiperda larvae). In 2012, it was shown to also inhibit fungi such as S. cerevisiae, C. parapsilosis, P. membranisfaciens at 9 uM and yeasts, C. tropicalis, K. marxiannus and C. albicans at 18 uM (Postal M et al., 2012). Membane permeation is the likely mechanism for inhibiting both insects and fungi. It seems that the N-terminal 44 residues are more important than the C-terminal portion (Martinelli AH et al., 2014). A helical region was found at the N-terminus. However, the peptide is largely diosordered, consistent with (15)N relaxation studies that revealed significant backbone mobility, especially in the N-terminal portion of the polypeptide (Lopes FC et al., 2015).

Crucial residues: Basic amino acids in the ring, ring size, fatty acid chain
Additional info: Chemical modification: Warning: the sequence is a close mimic of the natural peptide antibiotic. In the natural form, there are multiple Dab (2,4-diaminobutanoic acid), which are represented here as lysines. The molecule is cyclic due to the formation of an amide bond between the amino group of Dab in position 4 and the carboxyl group of the C-terminus. Polymyxin B is very similar (90%) to colistin with a change of F6 to L6. Activity: Polymyxin B is anti-film of P. mirabilis (Liu MC et al., 2012). BInds LPS:anti-inflammatory by supressing TNF-alpha released from murine RAW 264.7 cells and in vivo animal model:mouse:sepsis (see ref for AP3643). It also has antifungal activity in vivo (Zhai and Lin 2013). Antimicrobial robustness: KCl-insensitive:E. coli: 100 mM salt MIC 0.125 ug/ml, no change. Resistance mechanism: Bacteria have responding genes, and when knocked out, can reduce peptide MIC. Knock out lysX gene of C. pseudotuberculosis reduced the MIC substantially to 10 ug/ml (cf. 640 ug/ml with this gene) (Gill et al., 2023). For colistin-resistant K. pneumoniae, PhoP KO led to MIC decrease by 256 fold (DeBarro et al., 2025) Animal model:mouse: In thigh infection, antibacterial effect was well correlated with fAUC/MIC (R2 = 0.89). 2 log CFU was not achieved for any strain even at the highest MTD. There was no difference (P > 0.05) in antibacterial activity between polymyxin B and colistin with equimolar doses. In vivo PK:mouse: t1/2 to be added (Landersdorfer et al., 2018). AMPs in use: Polymyxin B is administered parenterally in its active form. Overall polymyxin B has superior clinical pharmacological properties compared with colistin or its prodrug (Nation et al. 2014). Updated 4/2018; 3/2020; 9/2023.

In a different case, Group A Streptococcus (GAS) has also been reported to be able to secrete protease ScpC to cleave LL-37 into LL8 and SK-29, reducing peptide chemotactic property rather than antibacterial activity. (resolution: 1.45 A): type II site (same defensin molecule): contacts of R17 and H35 with the phosphate of the PA headgroup. Also N28 and a carboxyl group of the acyl chain. Additional info: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals this sequence is most similar (60.71%) to SP-B P: 68%; K: 14%, R: 0%, G: 11%. A Pro-rich peptide without arginine. Name/Class: Bac7(1-35) (Synthetic AMPs, N-terminal fragment of Bac7, Arg-rich, Pro-rich; PrAMPs, UCLL1; BBL)
Crucial residues: N-terminal sequence
Additional info: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals this sequence is most similar (64.86%) to dolphin Tur1A P: 46%; R: 31%. GRAVY: -1.41; Mol Wt: 4207.161; Mol formula: C196H322N68O36; mol ex coeff: 0. Activity: active against parasite C. parvum in the form sporozoite but not oocyst. Active against E. coli ATCC 25922 or ML-35 (MIC 0.5 uM), S. enterica serovar Typhimurium ATCC 14028 (MIC 0.5 uM), S. marcescens ATCC8100 (MIC 1 uM), K. pneumoniae 13 clinical strains (MIC 0.25-1 uM), A. baumannii (12 clinical strains (MIC 0.5-16 uM), P. aeruginosa 20 clinical strains (MIC 0.5-32 uM), B-cepacia 10 clinical strains (MIC > 64 uM), S.aureus ATCC 25923 (MIC >128 uM), fungi C. neoformans (MIC 1-32 uM), P-etchellsii (MIC >32 uM), and C-albicans (MIC >64 uM) (Benincasa et al., 2004). It binds to LPS from Escherichia coli O111:B4. MOA:bacteria: SbmA is a bacterial inner membrane transporter required for importing the antimicrobial peptide (Runti et al., 2013). Bac7(1-35) binds to bacterial ribosomal proteins and inhibits protein synthesis (Mardirossian et al., 2014). Structure: the crystal structures of Bac7(1-35) bound to the Thermus thermophilus 70S ribosome has been determined (Gagnon et al., 2016). You can rotate, zoom, and view the 3D structure here in the PDB. Only residues 1-19 have coordinates. By removing the first 4 critical residues, peptide Bac7(5-35) can only stabilize the initiation complex at a high concentration of 100 uM, providing a structural basis to the importance of the N-terminal segment (Seefeldt AC et al., 2016). Animal model:rat: Bac7(1-35) completely inhibits the LPS procoagulant activity at approximately 10 uM and significant decrease in plasma LPS, thereby protecting the animals from the lethal effect of endotoxin (Ghiselli et al., 2003). Name/Class: BMAP-27-(1-18) (Synthetic AMPs, N-terminal fragment of BMAP-27, BMAP(1-18), Lys-rich; XXA, UCLL1c; BBMm; Variant: Bomidin, BMAP-15; BBMm; BBN)
Activity: Anti-Gram+ & Gram-, Antifungal, candidacidal, Antiparasitic, Anti-MRSA, Anti-inflammatory, Antibiofilm
Additional info: Nomenclature: originally named as BMAP-27-(1-18). A highly conserved single-residue variant (L17I) was made by Wang in 2008 for anti-HIV assays and named as BMAP-18. This name has been adopted in the literature since then to refer to this C-terminal fragment. Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals this sequence is most similar (66.67%) to BMAP-27 K: 39%; F: 22%; R: 17%. GRAVY: -1.28; M Wt: 2342.927; Mol formula: C113H188N34O20; mol ex coeff: 0. Activity: Active against E. coli ATCC 25922 ML-35 or D21 (MIC 2-4 uM), S. typhimurium ATCC 14028 (MIC 4 uM), P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 1-4 uM), S. marcescens ATCC 8100 (MIC 2 uM), S. aureus ATCC 25923 Cowan 1 or MRSA (MIC 2-4 uM), S. epidermidis ATCC 12228 (MIC 1-4 uM), B. megaterium Bm11 (MIC 2 uM), C. albicans (MIC 16 uM), and C. neoformans (MIC 4 uM). Recent MIC values have been merged with the previous data. Also inhibited biofilm formation at 16 uM and disrupted preformed biofilms at 8 uM. Also, active against parasite BSF and PCF of T. b. brucei (IC50 8-12 ug/ml), T. b. rhodesiense ViTat 1.1 PCF (IC50 ~30 ug/ml), T. b. gambiense U2 PCF (IC50 ~10 ug/ml), T. congolense IL3000 PCF (IC50 ~25 ug/ml), T. danilewskyi TrCa (IC50 ~32 ug/ml), and L. donovani LD3 (IC50 ~31 ug/ml) (Haines et al., 2009). Anti-inflammatory activity (supression of IL-6) is much weaker than LL-37 and its Leucine analog (AP3759). In vitro Toxicity: sheep RBC: not hemolytic until 20 uM. 20% hemolysis at 30-130 uM. HC50 at 16-32 uM to RAW264.7 mouse macrophages. Structure: it became helical in 0.1% LPS. MOA:bacteria: it targets membranes, especially Gram+ bacteria. SAR: BMAP-18 ( i.e. N-terminal 18-residues of BMAP-27) is HIV-active. Further deletion of three C-terminal residues from BMAP-18 led to a peptide (BMAP-15) that is inactive to HIV-1 (see ref). Surface immobilized peptides: BMAP-18 has been covalently linked to agarose beads or titanium surface with activity against S. epidermidis (Boix-Lemonche et al., 2019). Bomidin is a derivative of BMAP-18 with one additonal Met at the N-terminus. Bomidin inhibted V. parahaemolyticus, an important aquatic pathogen (PMID: 34642879).

Additional info: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (85.71%) to Dermaseptin-B3 L=A=K: 19%; G: 15%. GRAVY: 0.638; mol Wt: 2653.3; mol formula: C123H215N32O30S1; mol ex coeff: 5550. Chemical modification: Reduction of disulfide bonds and alkylation of cysteines indicate that disulfide bonds are important for peptide stability rather than activity. Activity: active against S. aureus NCTC 10788or MRSA NCTC 12493 (MIC 2 uM), E. faecalis NCTC 1269 (MIC 4 uM), E. coli NCTC 10418(MIC 2 uM), P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853 (MIC 2 uM), K. pneumoniae ATCC 43816 (MIC 1 uM) and C. albicans CYC 1467 (MIC 1 uM). Assays used 1 ul peptide/99 ul MHB culture. Inhibited cancer cells H157 (IC50 1.55 uM), MCF-7 (IC50 2.92 uM), PC-3 (IC50 4.15 uM), and U251 MG cells (IC50 2.47 uM). In vitro toxicity: horse RBC: HC50 38.77 uM. Induced a very low degree of LDH release in normal HMEC-1 cells (<10%). Structure: helical in 50% TFE. Peptide formulation: Animal model:mouse; wound healing model:S. aureus, formulated with polytannic acid (pTA)-coated PLGA nanoparticles could eliminate 99% E. coli and S. aureus in an irradiation controlled release manner (Guo et al., 2024). Promoted angiogenesis and reduced inflammation. Animal model:cancer:mouse: subcutaneous H157 tumor model: cancer cells injected into the right underarm to develop advanced tumor for 14 days. Treatment: daily intratumoral injections for 10 days, control treated with Cisplatin for 5 days IP. Sacrified day 11. Inhibited tumore growth in nude mice in a dose-dependent manner (tumor size reduced) without obviouss side effects. pH sensitive liposome formulation reduced toxicity and enhanced anticancer activity (Wang et al., 2023). MOA:cancer: Dermaseptin-PP Induced H157 Cell Apoptosis Through an Endogenous Mitochondrial Death Pathway.

Source: floral nectar, ornamental tobacco, a cross of N. sanderae and N. langsdorffii : hybrid species
Additional info: Discovery: pep6 was initially reported in 2022 (see ref). However, all the antifungal results below were reported in 2025 (Neto et al., 2025). Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is 42.11% similar to [I11A]tachyplesin I C=Y: 16%, H=K=R: 11%. GRAVY: -0.73; mol wt: 2422.84; mol formula: C110H157N32O25S3; mol ex coeff: 10207.5. Activity: Active against C.albicans ATCC 10231 (MIC 120 uM), C.krusei ATCC 22019 (MIC 133 uM), C.parapsilosis ATCC 6258 (MIC 141 uM), C. tropicalis INCQS 40042 (MIC 86 uM). Activity in the presence of 150 mM NaCl. In addition, the original report in 2022 showed that pep6 completely inhibited the growth of P. syringae pv. syringae, P. syringae pv. tomato, and X. perforans strains at 250 uM. MOA:fungi:C. albicans: act on membranes (PI indicator). Also ROS release. Structure: only formed helical structure in TFE (50%). Not helical in SDS (10 uM not enough?). In vitro toxicity: Human RBC: 28% hemolysis at 200 uM (poorly hemo.lytic). Cytotoxicity: not toxic at 200 uM. Animal model:Zebrafish: survival: 95% treated at 50 ug/ml (21 uM). zebrafish embryos: 40% survived. Embryo coagulation rates: LC50: 131 ug/mL (54 uM): not toxic. the lowest observed adverse effect level (LOAEL): 100 ug/ml.

Name/Class: P-113 (P113, Synthetic AMPs, histatin 5 fragment, XXA, UCLL1c; Derivative: P-113unam; P-113D, Nal-P-113, clinical)
Source: sequence truncation, human histatin analogs, animal-derived, natural derivative
Additional info: Sequence analysis: APD analysis reveals that this sequence is similar (50%) to human Histatin 5 H=K: 25%, R: 17%. Obtained by deletion of N-terminal DSH and C-terminal EKHHSHRGY of histatin 5. Chemical modification: different from other fragments in this study, this peptide is C-terminally amidated. Activity: active against C. albicans (LD50 2.3 ug/ml; LD90 4.7 ug/ml). Also active against 5 strains C. albican ATCC MYA-2876 or ATCC 90028 or 3 more from patients (MIC 0.78-12.5 ug/ml), C-glabrata ATCC 9003 (MIC >50 ug/ml), C. krusei ATCC 6258 or HIV patient (MIC 6.25-12.5 ug/ml), C. parapsilosis ATCC 22019 (MIC 0.78 ug/ml), C. tropicalis ATCC 13803 and 3 strains HIV patient (MIC 0.78-1.56 ug/ml), C. dubliniensis HIV patient (MIC 6.25 ug/ml), C. glabrata HIV patient (MIC 25 ug/ml). Both the D and L forms (D=L) were equally active against C. albicans, but only the D-form (P113-D) was active in vivo (Sajjan US et al 2001 Antimicrob Agents Chemother 45:3437-3444). Chemical modification: C-terminal amidation slightly increased peptide activity. P-113unam: without C-terminal amidation (LD50 3.9 ug/ml). P113D, synthesized using D-amino acids, retained the same antifungal activity. Structure: random coil in aqueous buffer and helical in 100% TFE. AMP inactivation: C. albicans can degrade intracellularly this peptide in normal L-amino acids, but not D-peptide (P-113D) (Ruissen et al., 2003). Clinical trials: P113 oral spray has the potential to reduce the dental caries and periodontal disease-related bacteria and to control the dental plaque formation (Wu et al., 2024). Also, Nal-P-113, where bulky amino acid beta-naphthylalanine replaces histidine, was subjected to clinical studies on periodontal pathogens and periodontal status. Inhibited the growth and biofilm formaiton of F. nucleatum, S. gordonii, T. denticola, and P. gingivalis in subgingival plaque (Wang et al., 2018). Updated 12/2025
